claim: On 2022-08-24 CloudFront added origin access control (OAC), which secures Amazon S3 origins by permitting access to only the designated CloudFront distributions.
question: When did CloudFront add origin access control for S3 origins?

qualifiers.scope: CloudFront origin access control for Amazon S3
qualifiers.condition: the What's New announcement is dated 2022-08-25

evidence.quote: | [Enhanced security with origin access control](private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.md) | You can now secure Amazon S3 origins by permitting access to only the designated CloudFront distributions. | August 24, 2022 |

note: d127. Older practice questions say 'use an origin access identity (OAI)'. See cloudfront-dec-oac-recommended-over-oai for the current best answer.

claim: On 2024-04-11 CloudFront added the ability to create an origin access control (OAC) for AWS Elemental MediaPackage V2 and AWS Lambda function URL origins, in addition to Amazon S3.
question: When did origin access control extend beyond S3 to Lambda function URLs?

values.display: AWS Elemental MediaPackage V2 and AWS Lambda function URL

evidence.quote: | [Added origin access control support](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-origin.html) | You can now create an origin access control (OAC) for AWS Elemental MediaPackage V2 and AWS Lambda function URL. | April 11, 2024 |

note: d127. FRESHNESS lists this date for 'OAC for Lambda function URLs'. CloudFront FAQ now lists S3, AWS Elemental and Lambda function URLs for OAC.

claim: On 2024-11-20 CloudFront added VPC origins, which restrict access to an Application Load Balancer, Network Load Balancer or EC2 instance origin.
question: When did CloudFront add VPC origins?

values.display: Application Load Balancer, Network Load Balancer, or EC2 instance origin

evidence.quote: | [VPC origins](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-vpc-origins.html) | Use CloudFront VPC origins to restrict access to an Application Load Balancer, Network Load Balancer, or EC2 instance origin. | November 20, 2024 |

note: d128. Older questions: public ALB plus secret header plus CloudFront prefix list. See cloudfront-dec-ddos-wp-vpc-origins-newest-recommended and the ELB fact elb-change-cloudfront-vpc-origins-2024-11.

claim: On 2024-11-20 CloudFront added Anycast static IPs, which you can request from CloudFront to use with your distributions.
question: When did CloudFront add Anycast static IPs?

values.display: request Anycast static IPs from CloudFront

evidence.quote: | [Anycast static IPs](request-static-ips.md) | You can request Anycast static IPs from CloudFront to use with your distributions. | November 20, 2024 |

note: d129. Static IP answers: before this date only Global Accelerator (and Elastic IP on a load balancer) gave static addresses. Global Accelerator stays the answer for non-HTTP TCP/UDP traffic and Regional failover.

claim: On 2025-04-28 CloudFront added multi-tenant distributions and distribution tenants, so that distribution tenants share the common settings of one multi-tenant distribution and can still be customized.
question: When did CloudFront add multi-tenant distributions?

evidence.quote: | [Added support for multi-tenant distribution and distribution tenants](distribution-config-options.md) | You can create a multi-tenant distribution to set common distribution settings based on your origin type. Then, you can reuse the multi-tenant distribution to create multiple distribution tenants that share those settings. You can then customize specific distribution tenants as you add additional websites or applications. | April 28, 2025 |

claim: On 2025-11-18 CloudFront added flat-rate pricing plans, to which you can subscribe your distributions.
question: When did CloudFront add flat-rate pricing plans?

values.display: subscribe your distributions to a CloudFront flat-rate pricing plan

qualifiers.condition: pay-as-you-go pricing stays available for each distribution

evidence.quote: | [CloudFront supports flat-rate pricing plans](flat-rate-pricing-plan.md) | You can now subscribe your distributions to a CloudFront flat-rate pricing plan. | November 18, 2025 |

This simplified pricing model is available alongside pay-as-you-go pricing for each CloudFront distribution, giving you the flexibility to choose the right pricing model and feature set for each application.

claim: On 2023-05-15 CloudFront added support for the Stale-While-Revalidate and Stale-If-Error cache control directives, which let it serve stale (expired) cache content.
question: When did CloudFront add stale-while-revalidate and stale-if-error?

qualifiers.condition: the What's New announcement is dated 2023-05-17

evidence.quote: | [Support for serving stale (expired) cache content](Expiration.md#stale-content) | CloudFront supports the `Stale-While-Revalidate` and `Stale-If-Error` cache control directives. | May 15, 2023 |
This directive allows CloudFront to serve stale content from the cache while CloudFront asynchronously fetches a fresh version from the origin.
This directive allows CloudFront to serve stale content from the cache if the origin is unreachable or returns an error code that is between 500 and 600.

note: d133. The two Expiration quotes state what each directive does today (the first is stale-while-revalidate, the second stale-if-error).

You can enable advanced customizable logic at CloudFront edge locations.  | November 21, 2023 |
